([[Daytona Beach, Florida]]) | college = [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] (2020–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 23 | draft_team = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]] | team2 = →[[Rip City Remix]] | years3 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team3 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | highlights = * {{nowrap|Third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Associated Press|AP]], [[USBWA]], ''[[Sporting News|SN]]'' ([[2023 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2023]])}} * First-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] (2023) }} '''Kristopher James Murray''' (born August 19, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa Hawkeyes]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]] from 2020 to 2023. He was first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] in his final year with the Hawkeyes. He is the twin brother of basketball player [[Keegan Murray]], who plays for the [[Sacramento Kings]]. ==Early life and high school career== Murray grew up in [[Cedar Rapids, Iowa]] and attended [[Prairie High School (Iowa)|Prairie High School]], where he played basketball with his twin brother [[Keegan Murray|Keegan]] as a teammate.{{cite web|url=https://www.thegazette.com/iowa-prep-sports/identical-twins-identical-numbers-keegan-and-kris-murray-help-cedar-rapids-prairie-to-great-season/|title=Identical twins, identical numbers: Keegan and Kris Murray help Cedar Rapids Prairie to great season|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|The Gazette]]|date=February 17, 2019|access-date=November 16, 2022}} He was named first team All-Metro and second team All-State after averaging 19.5 points, 6.4 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 2.5 blocks and 1.1 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://iowa.rivals.com/news/murray-twins-ready-to-live-their-dream|title=Murray twins ready to live their dream|first=Tom|last=Kakert|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=November 18, 2020|access-date=November 16, 2022}} Following graduation, Murray and his brother enrolled at [[DME Academy]] in [[Daytona Beach, Florida]] for a [[postgraduate year]].{{cite web|url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-basketball/iowa-commits-keegan-and-kris-murray-hit-home-run-at-dme-sports-academy/|title=Iowa commits Keegan and Kris Murray hit home run at DME Sports Academy|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|The Gazette]]|date=April 1, 2020|access-date=November 16, 2022}} Both brothers committed to playing college basketball for [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]].{{cite web|url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-basketball/keegan-and-kris-murray-commit-to-iowa-basketball-following-in-their-dads-footsteps/|title=Keegan and Kris Murray commit to Iowa basketball, following in their dad's footsteps|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|The Gazette]]|date=October 21, 2019|access-date=November 16, 2022}} ==College career== Murray played in 13 games, all off the bench, and 41 total minutes as a freshman for the Iowa Hawkeyes.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/iowa/basketball/kris-murray-ready-to-emerge|title=Kris Murray Looking to Build on Freshman Season|first=Rick|last=Brown|website=[[SI.com]]|date=October 19, 2021|access-date=November 16, 2022}} As a sophomore, he averaged 9.7 points and 4.3 rebounds over 35 games with one start.{{cite web|url=https://www.thegazette.com/iowa-basketball/its-kris-murrays-time-with-the-hawkeyes-and-hes-embracing-it/|title=It's Kris Murray's time with the Hawkeyes, and he's embracing it|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|The Gazette]]|date=July 19, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.ourquadcities.com/sports/hawkeye-headquarters/kris-murray-on-filling-brother-keegans-shoes-i-feel-no-pressure/|title=Kris Murray on filling brother Keegan's shoes: 'I feel no pressure'|first=Blake|last=Hornstein|website=[[WHBF-TV|OurQuadCities.com]]|date=October 5, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022|archive-date=December 1, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201194008/https://www.ourquadcities.com/sports/hawkeye-headquarters/kris-murray-on-filling-brother-keegans-shoes-i-feel-no-pressure/|url-status=dead}} Following the end of the season, Murray entered the [[2022 NBA draft]] after his brother had already done so.{{cite web|url=https://www.thegazette.com/hawkeye-basketball/iowa-hawkeyes-kris-murray-declares-for-nba-draft-but-it-doesnt-mean-hes-leaving-hawkeyes/|title=Iowa Hawkeyes' Kris Murray declares for NBA draft, but it doesn't mean he's leaving Hawkeyes|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|The Gazette]]|date=April 14, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022}} He ultimately withdrew his name from the draft shortly after declining an invitation to the [[NBA draft combine]].{{cite web|url=https://qctimes.com/sports/college/basketball/keegan-murray-comfortable-with-draft-decision/article_d90e9dbb-a8c2-5aa8-9e61-0ce255c20199.html|title=Keegan Murray comfortable with draft decision|work=[[Quad-City Times]]|date=May 28, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://cbs2iowa.com/sports/hawkeye-xtra/kris-murray-declines-invitation-to-nba-draft-combine|title=Kris Murray declines invitation to NBA Draft Combine|first=Owen|last=Siebring|website=[[KGAN|CBS2Iowa.com]]|date=May 10, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022}} Murray entered his junior season at Iowa on the watchlists for the [[Karl Malone Award]] and the [[John R. Wooden Award]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Iowa-Basketball-Kris-Murray-Named-to-Karl-Malone-Award-watch-list-196220622/|title=Iowa Basketball: Kris Murray named to Karl Malone Award watch list|first=David|last=Eickholt|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=October 27, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/iowa/basketball/wooden-award-watch-list-includes-kris-murray|title=Wooden Award Watch List Includes Kris Murray|website=[[SI.com]]|date=November 15, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022}} He averaged 20.2 points, 7.9 rebounds and 2 assists per game and was named first-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] at the end of the season. Murray was also named a third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[Associated Press]], [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] and the ''[[Sporting News]]''.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/iowa/Article/Iowa-Basketball-Kris-Murray-named-consensus-all-American-207448025/|title=Iowa Basketball: Kris Murray named consensus all-American|first=David|last=Eickholt|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=March 28, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023}} After the season, he entered the [[2023 NBA draft]], where he was selected 23rd overall by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4390520/2023/04/07/iowa-kris-murray-nba-draft/|title=Iowa’s Kris Murray declares for NBA Draft: Where is he projected to be picked?|first1=Sam|last1=Vecenie|first2=Eamonn|last2=Brennan|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=April 7, 2023|access-date=April 11, 2023|via=The New York Times}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2023–2026)=== Murray was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the first round of the [[2023 NBA draft]] with the 23rd overall pick{{cite web|first=Aaron|last=Fentress|title=Trail Blazers select Iowa forward Kris Murray with No. 23 pick in 2023 NBA draft|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/sports/2023/06/trail-blazers-select-iowa-forward-kris-murray-with-no-23-pick-in-2023-nba-draft.html|work=[[The Oregonian]]|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 23, 2023}} and on July 1, 2023, he signed with the Blazers.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Scoot Henderson and Kris Murray|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-scoot-henderson-and-kris-murray|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2023|access-date=November 12, 2023}} He scored back-to-back career-highs in points in consecutive games against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on March 20 and March 22, posting 17 and then 21 points.{{Cite web |date=2024-03-21 |title=Trail Blazers' Kris Murray: Posts career-high point total |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/trail-blazers-kris-murray-posts-career-high-point-total/ |access-date=2024-03-23 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}{{cite web | last=Holdahl | first=Casey | title=Rally Falls Short In Second Contest Versus Clippers | website=NBA.com | date=2024-03-23 | url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/rally-falls-short-in-second-contest-versus-clippers | access-date=2025-12-06}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2026–present)=== On June 29, 2026, Murray was traded to the
